text: Which genes specific to either tongue or esophagus are enhanced in suprabasal keratinocytes (single-cell), have no detectable mRNA in liver, and are not cancer-related genes?
plan: Tissue category (RNA): Esophagus, Tongue / Tissue enriched AND Cell type category (scRNA): Suprabasal keratinocytes / Cell type enhanced AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected AND NOT Protein class: Cancer-related genes
understanding: The user is querying the Human Protein Atlas for genes based on tissue-specific RNA expression (tongue or esophagus), single-cell RNA-seq enhancement in suprabasal keratinocytes, lack of detectable mRNA in liver, and exclusion from the cancer-related gene class.

trail.requirement: specific to either tongue or esophagus
trail.why: Tissue enriched identifies genes specific to a particular tissue by requiring at least four-fold higher mRNA levels compared to any other tissue.
The requirement specifies genes that are enhanced in suprabasal keratinocytes, which corresponds directly to selecting 'Suprabasal keratinocytes' at Level 1 and 'Cell type enhanced' at Level 2.

trail.requirement: have no detectable mRNA in liver
trail.why: Filtering for 'liver' at Level 1 and 'Not detected' at Level 2 precisely identifies genes with mRNA below the detection cut-off in liver tissue.
Selecting the class 'Cancer-related genes' covers all cancer-related genes without restricting to a specific subclass.

requirements.requirement: specific to either tongue or esophagus
requirements.why: Tissue category (RNA) classifies genes by RNA specificity across human tissues, allowing selection of genes specific to esophagus and/or tongue.
Cell type category (scRNA) covers RNA specificity categories across 81 single-cell types, which includes suprabasal keratinocytes.

requirements.requirement: have no detectable mRNA in liver
requirements.why: Tissue category (RNA) classifies tissue distribution and detection levels of mRNA across human tissues, including liver.
Protein class categorizes functional and disease gene groups including cancer-related genes, and NOT excludes genes in this class.
